title: African Development Bank approves €20m for low-carbon cement complex in Côte d’Ivoire
summary: African Development Bank approves €20m for low-carbon cement complex in Côte d’Ivoire
body_markdown:
**Côte d’Ivoire:** The African Development Bank Group has approved €20m in financing for Ciments écologiques de Côte d’Ivoire (CIMECI), a YESHI Group company, to build a low-carbon cement production complex in Attingué, north of Abidjan. The complex will include a calcined-clay plant with a capacity of approximately 0.35Mt/yr and a grinding plant capable of producing up to 0.5Mt/yr of cement. The project aims to reduce reliance on imported clinker and lower production-related CO₂ emissions.


Solomon Quaynor, African Development Bank Group vice-president for private sector, infrastructure and industrialisation, said “The project demonstrates how locally available raw materials, private capital and lower-carbon technology can work together to strengthen domestic industry.”


Khalid Iben Khayat, YESHI Group managing director of industry, said “The technology will significantly reduce CO₂ emissions from cement production compared with those of traditional, clinker-intensive cement.”
